items.stem: Define the term 'liquidity'.
items.answer: The ability of a business to pay its short-term debts as they fall due.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the ability of a business to pay its short-term debts as they fall due. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a very high current ratio is not necessarily good.
items.answer: It may mean too much money is tied up in idle cash, excess inventory or slow-paying receivables that could be used more profitably.
items.markingKey: 1 mark idle resources; 1 mark opportunity cost/profitability. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a supermarket can operate with a current ratio below 1.
items.answer: It sells inventory quickly for cash but pays suppliers on credit, so cash flows in before payables fall due.
items.markingKey: 1 mark fast inventory turnover/cash sales; 1 mark credit from suppliers. [2]

items.stem: Based in Lisbon, Tejo Mobility SA (public limited company) assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. The business has around 600 employees. Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Explain the reasons why Tejo Mobility's current ratio might have fallen over the last year.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tejo Mobility: current ratio = CA ÷ CL; cash used for investment in non-current assets; more short-term borrowing or overdraft; trade payables rising as purchases grow.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: current ratio = CA ÷ CL. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Tejo Mobility: vehicle manufacturing, about 600 employees, public limited company in Portugal; battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Tejo Mobility, e.g. cash used for investment in non-current assets; more short-term borrowing or overdraft; trade payables rising as purchases grow. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Explain the reasons why Lumen Robotics' current ratio might have fallen over the last year.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lumen Robotics: current ratio = CA ÷ CL; cash used for investment in non-current assets; more short-term borrowing or overdraft; trade payables rising as purchases grow.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: current ratio = CA ÷ CL. items.stem: Café Cordillera SAS is a private limited company based in Bogotá, Colombia. It roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés and employs about 900 people. The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Explain how a fall in Café Cordillera's acid test ratio could affect the business.
items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: acid test = liquid assets ÷ current liabilities; harder to pay suppliers and short-term debts; suppliers and banks may restrict credit; may need costly short-term finance.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: acid test = liquid assets ÷ current liabilities. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Café Cordillera: food and drink retail, about 900 employees, private limited company in Colombia; the owners want to double the number of cafés within three years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Café Cordillera, e.g. harder to pay suppliers and short-term debts; suppliers and banks may restrict credit; may need costly short-term finance. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Seoul, Han River Games Co. (private limited company) develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. The business has around 340 employees. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Evaluate the best way for Han River Games to improve its liquidity.
items.answer: For: sale and leaseback releases large sums; reducing inventory releases cash; faster collection of receivables. Against: loss of assets and lease costs; stock-outs; tighter credit may lose customers. Judgement: the decision for Han River Games depends mainly on the size and urgency of the problem, and also on the cause of the low liquidity.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Han River Games: video game development, about 340 employees, private limited company in South Korea; one game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. sale and leaseback releases large sums; reducing inventory releases cash; faster collection of receivables; arguments against, e.g. loss of assets and lease costs; stock-outs; tighter credit may lose customers. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the size and urgency of the problem; the cause of the low liquidity; its long-term plans. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Han River Games, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Why does the acid test ratio exclude inventory?
options: Inventory may not be easily or quickly converted into cash
items.answer: Inventory may not be easily or quickly converted into cash
items.markingKey: Inventory may not be easily or quickly converted into cash. Inventory is the least liquid current asset.

items.stem: Explain two ways a business could improve its liquidity.
items.answer: Sell surplus assets or inventory; chase receivables; sale and leaseback; convert short-term debt into long-term loans; raise share capital.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark method, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Andina Solar SpA has inventory $3.75m, trade receivables $1.75m, cash $1m and current liabilities $7.8m. Calculate the current ratio and the acid test ratio.
items.answer: Current ratio 0.83; acid test 0.35

items.stem: BatikPay Sdn Bhd is a private limited company based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops and employs about 210 people. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. (a) Define 'acid test ratio'. (b) Explain one advantage to BatikPay of reducing its inventory levels to improve liquidity.
items.answer: (a) (Current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities; a stricter liquidity measure that excludes inventory because it may be hard to turn into cash quickly. (b) Releases cash.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (releases cash; lower storage costs; less risk of obsolescence), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to BatikPay [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'return on capital employed (ROCE)'.
items.answer: Operating profit ÷ capital employed × 100, where capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities; measures how well the business uses its long-term capital.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, operating profit ÷ capital employed × 100, where capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities; measures how well the business uses its long-term capital. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why ROCE is often regarded as the most important profitability ratio.
items.answer: It compares operating profit with the capital invested, so it shows the return on all long-term finance and can be compared with interest rates and other firms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark profit relative to capital; 1 mark comparison use. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a business could reduce its trade receivables days.
items.answer: Offer discounts for early payment, tighten credit checks and terms, chase late payers, or use debt factoring.
items.markingKey: 1 mark method; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Nusantara Apparel Tbk, a public limited company in Indonesia with about 4,000 employees, makes sportswear under contract for global brands. Explain how Nusantara Apparel could improve its inventory turnover.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory; JIT and better forecasting reduce stock; removing slow-moving lines; promotions to sell excess inventory.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Nusantara Apparel, e.g. JIT and better forecasting reduce stock; removing slow-moving lines; promotions to sell excess inventory. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: ROCE = operating profit ÷ capital employed; falling margins from rising costs or price cuts; new investment not yet earning returns; less efficient use of assets.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: ROCE = operating profit ÷ capital employed. items.answer: For: show inventory and credit control; comparisons over time; link to cash flow. Against: ignore quality and customer service; industry differences; based on year-end figures. items.answer: Attracts and keeps customers.

items.stem: Data for Mekong Furniture JSC ($m): revenue 2.4; cost of sales 1.44; operating profit 0.36; capital employed 1.8; opening inventory 0.18; closing inventory 0.198; trade receivables 0.24; trade payables 0.216. Calculate the return on capital employed.

Data for Lagos Bites Ltd ($m): revenue 9; cost of sales 4.5; operating profit 3.15; capital employed 15.75; opening inventory 0.36; closing inventory 0.396; trade receivables 1.08; trade payables 0.45. Calculate the ROCE, the inventory turnover and the trade receivables days.
items.answer: ROCE 20%; inventory turnover 11.9 times; receivables 43.8 days
items.markingKey: ROCE = 3.15/15.75 × 100 = 20% [1]; average inventory = 0.378, turnover = 4.5/0.378 = 11.9 times [1]; receivables days = 1.08/9 × 365 = 43.8 days [1]. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'gearing ratio'.
items.answer: Non-current liabilities ÷ capital employed (total equity + non-current liabilities) × 100; the proportion of long-term finance that comes from borrowing.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, non-current liabilities ÷ capital employed (total equity + non-current liabilities) × 100; the proportion of long-term finance that comes from borrowing. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a highly geared business is more at risk when interest rates rise.
items.answer: Most of its capital is borrowed, so higher rates raise interest costs sharply, reducing profit and possibly making repayments difficult.
items.markingKey: 1 mark large debt; 1 mark interest cost/profit effect. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a low dividend cover may concern shareholders.
items.answer: Most of the profit is paid out, so little is retained for investment and the dividend may be cut if profits fall.
items.markingKey: 1 mark little retained/at risk; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.markingKey: 50%. Gearing above 50% means more than half of capital employed is borrowed.

items.answer: Shareholders keep control.

items.stem: Define the term 'ratio analysis'.
items.answer: Comparing figures from the financial statements as ratios to assess a business's profitability, liquidity, efficiency, gearing and returns to shareholders.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, comparing figures from the financial statements as ratios to assess a business's profitability, liquidity, efficiency, gearing and returns to shareholders. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why ratios should be compared over time and with other firms.
items.answer: A single ratio has little meaning; trends show improvement or decline, and inter-firm comparison shows performance relative to competitors.
items.markingKey: 1 mark trend; 1 mark inter-firm. [2]

items.stem: Explain two limitations of using ratio analysis to judge a business.
items.answer: Historic data; different accounting policies; window dressing; inflation; ignores qualitative factors such as staff morale or brand strength.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark limitation, 1 mark explanation). [4]
